title: OmniVideo-R1: Reinforcing Audio-visual Reasoning
one_liner: OmniVideo-R1 improves video reasoning by learning which parts of a question need audio, which need video, and how strongly each modality should influence the answer.
lead: Video understanding is harder than image understanding because the answer may depend on synchronized evidence across sound and motion. A question about whether a person is calling for help, playing an instrument, or operating a machine cannot be solved by video frames alone or audio alone in many cases because one stream may show the action while the other stream confirms what event is actually happening. OmniVideo-R1 treats multimodal reasoning as two linked decisions: identify what the question is asking for, then assign more weight to the modalities that contain that evidence.

problem.h2: Mixed-modality questions fail when the model does not know which evidence source matters most
paras: Omnivideo tasks mix several evidence types: visual actions over time, spoken words, background sounds, and their alignment. Existing systems often fuse these streams in a fixed way, which means they apply similar weight to audio and video across many questions even when the question strongly favors one modality.

That fixed treatment creates two failures. First, the model may look at the wrong source. A question about what sound occurred can be overwhelmed by visual motion. Second, the model may fail to combine the sources when both are needed. For example, identifying whether a visible instrument is actually being played requires both the motion and the sound. Good reasoning therefore needs query-dependent grounding and query-dependent fusion.

callout.html: A multimodal video model needs to know not only what is in the streams, but which stream should dominate for this question and when the streams must be combined.

panels.title: 1. Video and audio arrive together
panels.caption: The input contains motion, appearance, spoken content, and background sound.

panels.title: 2. Question selects the evidence demand
panels.viz_args: Some questions are audio-heavy, some video-heavy, and some require both.
panels.caption: The model first has to infer what evidence the question is asking for.

panels.title: 3. Query grounding locates useful cues
panels.caption: The system aligns the question with the most informative parts of the streams.

panels.title: 4. Fusion weights the modalities
panels.viz_args: Audio and video contributions are scaled according to the query.
panels.caption: The model combines modalities with variable emphasis rather than fixed mixing.

panels.title: 5. Final answer uses the right mixture
panels.caption: The answer improves because the evidence combination matches the question's true demand.

steps.text: The system starts with representations of the sound track, the visual frames, and the query.
It estimates whether the question mainly depends on audio, mainly on video, or on joint evidence.

steps.b: Ground the query in each modality
steps.text: Self-supervised training teaches the model to align the query with informative regions or time segments without requiring full manual labels, where self-supervised means the training signal is built from the data itself rather than from hand-written answers at every step.

Contrastive learning teaches the model to bring matching audio-video-query triples closer and separate mismatched ones, where contrastive learning means learning by comparing matching examples against non-matching examples.
Reinforcement favors answer trajectories that use the right modality balance for the question.

paras: The paper changes multimodal fusion from fixed combination to question-conditioned combination. It also trains an explicit query-grounding stage before fusion. Together, these changes make the model decide what kind of evidence the question requires before it decides how much each modality should contribute.

hidden.name: modality relevance
paras: Modality relevance measures how useful each stream is for the current question. A question about a spoken phrase should assign high relevance to audio. A question about hand movement should assign high relevance to video. A question about whether the visible action matches the sound should assign high relevance to both.

This quantity matters because fusion is only correct if it matches the evidence demand. If audio and video are averaged in the same way for every question, one stream can dilute the informative one. OmniVideo-R1 therefore learns to estimate relevance first and use it to control fusion later.

heat.caption: Darker means that evidence source is more relevant to the current query.

reads.html: The model asks which stream carries the answer for this question and how much each stream should count.
OmniVideo-R1 couples query grounding with modality-attentive fusion so that answer generation depends on question-specific evidence allocation.

mechanism.h2: Why query intention and modality weighting improve audio-visual reasoning
paras: The first mechanism is query-intensive grounding. The model learns to align the question with informative segments in each modality before final fusion. This helps because the system does not treat every frame and every sound segment equally; it narrows focus to the parts that could answer the query.

The second mechanism is modality-attentive fusion. Instead of using a fixed merge, the model estimates how much audio and video should contribute for this question. That improves answers because the more relevant stream is amplified and the less relevant stream is restrained, so noisy or distracting evidence has less influence on the final reasoning state.

The third mechanism is reinforcement over mixed-modality reasoning. Reinforcement trains from answer outcomes on sampled reasoning trajectories. If the model answers correctly by assigning strong weight to audio on sound-centric questions and joint weight on alignment questions, those patterns receive more credit. Over time, the policy learns a stable mapping from query intention to modality weighting.

stages.s: Audio stream, video stream, and question
Infer what evidence the question needs
Ground the query within each modality
Answer based on the right audio-video mixture

math.words: The final reasoning state is a weighted sum of audio and video evidence, where the weights depend on the question.
symbols: the combined representation used to answer the question
how much the audio stream should influence the answer for this query

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Question: Is the person playing the piano or only sitting near it?
Suppose the query grounding finds strong piano sound and visible hand motion on the keys.
Set audio_weight = 0.6 and video_weight = 0.4 because sound is slightly more decisive here.
If audio_evidence = 8 and video_evidence = 6, then final_state = 0.6 * 8 + 0.4 * 6 = 7.2.
If the question were only 'What instrument is visible?', the weights would shift toward video because the evidence demand changed.

math.note: The key idea is that the weights are not fixed properties of the model; they are outputs conditioned on the current query.

charts.title: Fixed audio-video fusion
charts.note: A fixed mixture cannot adapt to question demand, so it underuses the decisive stream and overuses the distractor stream.

charts.title: OmniVideo-R1 query-conditioned fusion
charts.note: The gains come from estimating modality relevance first and then using that estimate to control how evidence is combined.

items.html: If the model decides a question is video-heavy when the answer depends on sound, fusion will amplify the wrong stream and the later stages cannot fully repair that mistake.
If the audio segment and video segment selected for the question do not correspond to the same event, the fused state mixes unrelated evidence and produces unstable answers.
If mismatched examples are too easy to separate, the model may not learn fine distinctions about which modality pairing truly supports the query.
The model first identifies the evidence demand, then grounds each stream, then fuses them with query-dependent weights that reflect that demand.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a toy video dataset with three question types: audio-only, video-only, and joint audio-video alignment. For each clip, provide one correct audio track and optionally a mismatched track. Train one model with fixed fusion and another with learned query-conditioned weights. Measure answer accuracy by question type, whether the dominant modality weight matches the question type, and whether alignment questions fail when audio and video are intentionally mismatched.
demo.closing: The demo should show that the gain is not merely from adding more modalities, but from deciding which modality matters for the current query and weighting it accordingly.
